articleTitle: Predicting Battery State of Charge: A Machine Learning-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper aims to predict Battery SOC using a machine learning-based approach, employing three distinct methods: Random Forest Regression, Gradient Boosting Regression, and Artificial Neural Networks. The state of charge (SOC) is a critical battery parameter for electric vehicles (EVs), as it indicates the remaining driving range and battery health. Traditional methods frequently face challenges in delivering precise and real-time State of Charge (SOC) estimates. This is due to the intricate and dynamic battery behavior, compounded by variations in driving conditions and ambient temperature. A publicly available dataset of a BMW i3 (60Ah) EV, which contains data from 70 real driving trips in summer and winter season have been utilized for model training & testing. We evaluated the accuracy and robustness of these methods using various statistical metrics and graphical plots. The machine learning models developed in this paper are able to achieve prediction accuracy of more than ${9 8 \%}$ in case of RFR & GBR and $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ in case of ANN. The proposed approach can provide a fast and reliable way to predict battery SOC for EVs, and can be extended to other types of batteries and applications.

articleTitle: Cascaded H-Bridge 15 Level Inverter with Reduced Switch Count
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The Multilevel inverter is commonly employed for the DC–AC adaptation for high-power applications, it attracts more problems and research interest. In a traditional multilevel converter, there are more levels as there are power switches. The effectiveness of this multi-level stepped output waveform is measured in Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and the quantity of power switches. For medium power applications, this study suggests a fifteen-level inverter with fewer power switches and simplified PWM generation. Each output voltage level in the proposed system uses fewer switches for conduction. The THD is minimal when using the modified PWM approach. Using MATLAB-Simulink the computer-based simulation model is developed.

articleTitle: Accident Alert and Vehicle Theft Intimation System Using GSM Modem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In the contemporary landscape of automotive safety and security, the Accident Alert and Vehicle Theft Intimation System using GSM Modem stands as a pivotal innovation. This research paper delves into the design, implementation, and evaluation of this system, which integrates GSM communicationtechnology, sensors, and microcontrollers to detect accidents and unauthorized vehicle movements swiftly. Upon detection using GPS Modem, the system autonomously triggers SMS alerts to predefined recipients, such as emergency services and vehicle owners, facilitating prompt response and mitigation of potential damages. The paper investigates the system’s effectiveness in enhancing road safety, preventing vehiclethefts, and minimizing the impact of accidents. Furthermore, it explores the system’s applicability acrossdiverse contexts and its potential implications for future advancements in automotive security technologies. Through rigorous analysis and experimentation, this research contributes to the ongoing discourse on leveraging technology to ensure the safety and security ofvehicles and their occupants.

articleTitle: Read Right: Empowering the Blind to Read the World
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In the real world, knowledge comes from books and papers. Now that information only reaches to those with clear vision. In the community there are a part of people suffering either from poor eyesight or blindness. Braille is one of the methods employed to interpret several reports or books, however obtaining all these files in braille may be prohibitively expensive as well as regularly impossible. Hence, considering these issues and flaws in existing systems this paper is designed as a simple user-friendly mobile application “Read Right” that works on voice commands like “Take Picture” to click an image of the document which extracts text from picture as well plays it out (audio) also providing futuristic object detection. All this is designed using Firebase ML kit which predominantly uses bitmap class for preprocessing, text-to-speech synthesizer and FirebaseVisionObjectDetector, for joining machine learning capabilities into portable applications. Hence, the application stands out for its flexibility in dealing with official archives through voice.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition using Image Filtering Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In the present era, facial emotion recognition is one of the rapidly growing research fields that have various applications like human-computer interaction, security, health care, and human resource management. Facial expressions represent person’s emotional state. In this paper, the Butterworth filter is utilized to filter the image before sending it to CNN architecture. Recognition accuracy of the model without using the Butterworth filter is $\mathbf{9 8. 0 5 \%}$. In the proposed model images of the CK+ dataset have been pre-processed using the Butterworth filter, and then the dataset has been trained using the CNN model, which comprises two convolution layers and two max pooling layers. Analyzing emotions in images using proposed CNN model we have achieved improved test accuracy for various orders and cut off frequencies of Butterworth filter such as for order 4,5 and 6 with cut off frequency 25 model achieved test accuracy of $99.35 \%, 100 \%$, and $99.35 \%$ respectively.

articleTitle: Digital Stage for Surplus Food Redistribution: Undertaking Food Waste Through Online Donations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: To increase a Web Based software that reduces the quantity of meals wastage produced in restaurants, capabilities and mess. The contemporary gadget most effective presents statistics on the quantity of meals wasted and does now no longer offer an interface to donate and offer records evaluation. Using records evaluation, to visualize the effect. Donating the extra meals that includes the subsequent information, first, offering the region of in which extra meals is available & information of the meals amount available. Immediate Alerts to close by NGO‘s, orphanage, volunteers to accumulate them. According to a current survey, 1.3 billion lots of meals is being wasted every yr and one $1 / 3$ of meals ate up are leftover. To produce a gadget that reduces the quantity of meals being wasted, the focal point of the task is to increase internet software that makes use of records evaluation to visualize the effect of extra meals, for that reason decreasing meals wastage. It additionally permits to provide away the extra meals produced via way of means of notifying the close by users (NGO‘s, Volunteers) with information of the meals available.

articleTitle: Implementing Newly Proposed Dynamic Tree Structure: Development, Integration, and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: An innovative data structure called a “dynamic tree” has important uses in algorithmic time complexity optimization. It creates well-organized trees by modifying the properties of several single-node trees, therefore preserving the forest structure. This structure is essential to improving the effectiveness of many algorithms. In this work, I particularly address the “Maximum Flow method,” a crucial subtopic in the larger field of dynamic trees. One basic method for solving network flow issues is the Maximum Flow Algorithm, but it frequently runs into issues with time complexity. My research attempts to overcome these obstacles by using dynamic trees to enhance the efficiency of the algorithm. This work reduces the time complexity of network flow problems, leading to more effective solutions. The findings have potential implications in a variety of computing and real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Mortality Prediction through Machine Learning: Insights from XGBoost and Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This study explores the use of machine learning algorithms to predict deaths caused by different risk factors in various countries. Using a large dataset that covers many years and regions, we applied models like XGBoost and Random Forest to see how well they could predict death rates based on health and environmental factors. The XGBoost model was very accurate with an $\text{R}^{2}$ of $\mathbf{0. 9 9 5 6}$, showing it could explain most of the variability in death rates. The Random Forest model also performed well with an $\text{R}^{2}$ of 0.9926. These findings show that machine learning can be very useful in health analysis, helping to understand the risk factors that lead to higher death rates. The study discusses how these results can inform public health policies and guide future research.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Neural Network-Based Routing Algorithms for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are integral to diverse applications, including environmental monitoring, healthcare, and smart city infrastructure. The efficiency of data routing within these networks is crucial for optimizing performance and extending the lifespan of sensor nodes. This paper presents a comparative study between neural network-based routing algorithms and traditional protocols in WSNs. The analysis focuses on key performance metrics such as energy consumption, packet delivery ratio, and end-to-end delay across various network scenarios. Our findings highlight the advantages of employing neural networks, which can adapt to dynamic network conditions, thereby enhancing overall efficiency. The study emphasizes the potential of integrating machine learning techniques into WSN routing protocols, offering more intelligent, responsive, and energy-efficient network management solutions. The results suggest a promising future for machine learning-driven approaches in WSNs, with future research opportunities including the exploration of advanced machine learning models and their applicability in large-scale and heterogeneous WSN deployments. This work contributes to the evolving landscape of WSNs, aiming to support the development of smarter and more sustainable networks.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Ripeness Level and Shelf-Life Time Prediction for Custard Apples
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Food wastage stands as a prominent global concern, Many food processing industries have turned to smart automated systems to minimize human error. This study seeks to develop a deep learning-based system focused on evaluating the ripeness of custard apples and predicting their remaining shelf-life. The proposed system aims to be user-friendly, adaptable and will be integrated with mobile phone applications or edge devices which makes it easy to use by food processing industries as well as the general public. The system consists of one mobile application with UI to capture the image and show the result to the user and two deep learning-based models, first is object detection model based on YOLOv5s architecture to detect the ripeness level of custard apple and other is EfficientNet-B0 classification model which classify the custard apple into its expected shelf-life day. The proposed model for ripeness level detection achieves ${9 3 \%}$ accuracy and shelf-life day prediction model achieves ${9 2. 7 \%}$ accuracy. Additionally, the mean squared error and mean absolute error for remaining shelf-life day prediction were calculated to be 0.0854 and 0.0769, respectively. These results suggest the potential effectiveness of the developed system in addressing food quality and wastage concerns, offering practical benefits to both industry stakeholders and consumers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fraud Detection in Ethereum Transactions: Fusion of Modified Genetic Algorithms and Deep Learning with Limited Attributes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Ethereum smart contracts, the new way of transactions and a popular name in the world of cryptocurrencies, have gathered a huge base of research and scientific attention. They are so helpful that they allow us to eliminate the need for a separate third-party library to allow unknown parties to see contract details on a computer. But since we can all see that online commerce is growing day by day and will continue to grow, it can never be fully free from scams and unethical operations. So, to correctly detect all such unethical and malicious transactions, this paper used a deep learning model. And to further enhance the model, this study used metaheuristic optimization as well. It employs an algorithm called Genetic Algorithm and to provide better optimization in the explorations phase of Cuckoo Search (CS) to achieve its goal of detecting fraudulent transactions. The algorithm covers the loopholes in the CS strategy. Furthermore, to provide strong grounds for research in our paper, this proposed model was compared with various types of approaches such as Light Gradient Boosting Machine, Support Vector Classification, Multi-Layer Perceptron, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest. The proposed model outperforms other significant models like SVC, KNN, LGBM Classifier, RF etc. with the accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 6 \%}$.

articleTitle: Diabetes Prediction Using Machine Learning: A Comparative Analyses of Classification Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic metabolic condition identified by increased levels of sugar in the blood. It is also commonly referred to as diabetes mellitus. Either inadequate insulin production or inadequate insulin use by the organism cause this condition. Early identification and prediction of the onset of diabetes can lead to timely interventions and improved patient outcomes. In an effort to increase the precision and effectiveness of machine learning predictive models, this research article provides a thorough analysis of diabetes prediction utilizing these techniques. The study utilizes a diverse dataset comprising of 768 observations, lifestyle factors, and clinical indicators obtained from a cohort of individuals with and without diabetes. Feature selection methods are employed to identify the most relevant variables, ensuring a robust and parsimonious model. Various machine learning algorithms are implemented and compared to determine the optimal predictive model.

articleTitle: Spotting Deep Fakes: Exploring Detection Techniques for Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The birth of the Deep Fake technology has got into the system like a parasite in a new world of digital manipulation, and this poses profound challenges to the integrity of multimedia content. The following paper undertakes a comprehensive examination of the insights on principles and methodologies employed in recognizing Deep Fakes from authentic media assets. At the heart of the detection challenge lies the inherent differences in the generation processes of Deep Fakes compared to genuine content, necessitating the development of specialized detection techniques. Multiple approaches have been proposed, enclosing both traditional and cutting - edge methodologies. As deep learning has taken its place at the forefront of technology, there is an upgrade in deep fake detection. The rapid advancement in artificial intelligence has given rise to Deep Fake technology, capable of producing highly realistic but fabricated multimedia content. This technology poses significant threats to the authenticity and integrity of digital media, making the development of effective detection mechanisms crucial. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of various detection techniques, with a focus on deep learning-based models that enhance the accuracy and reliability of identifying manipulated content. Many potent tools like CNNs(Convolutional neural networks, RNNs(recurrent neural networks), and GNNs (Generative Adversarial Networks) have arisen to help distinguish the features or patterns of the Deep fakes.

articleTitle: Advanced Energy Flow and Power Quality Management in a Wind-PV-Battery Microgrid: AI-Driven Modelling and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive Analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for advanced energy flow and power quality management in wind-PV-battery microgrids. The study compares optimization, machine learning, and multi-agent approaches for microgrid energy management and explores AI-driven modeling of wind turbines, PV systems, and batteries to capture complex nonlinearities and uncertainties. AI-based control strategies for voltage and frequency regulation, harmonic mitigation, and reactive power compensation are investigated, highlighting their strengths and limitations. The paper identifies research gaps and future directions, emphasizing the need for scalable, secure, and resilient AI systems for large-scale microgrid energy management. Hybrid AI methods incorporating optimization, learning, and multi-agent approaches are recommended. The study concludes that AI enables intelligent, adaptive, and autonomous operation of renewable-rich microgrids, contributing to a more sustainable and reliable energy future. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of AI-based control techniques in improving power quality and energy management in microgrids.

articleTitle: OpenCv Based Enhanced Criminal Identification Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This study examines how a facial recognition system might be used in real-world situations to demonstrate its efficacy. The core operation of this system is ensured by meticulously selected datasets that comprise categorized photos. An important part is a carefully constructed file called “simple faces,” which is optimized for necessary libraries such as glob, OS, NumPy, OpenCV, and OS. Important tasks like image processing and matching faces to their corresponding photos are made easier by these frameworks. The study also emphasizes the significance of having a specific file for face detection and uses OpenCV to locate facial features precisely. In addition, a sophisticated face recognition library with strong features detection, encoding, and comparison capabilities is used. This library uses CNNs and other cutting-edge pretrained deep learning models to deliver exceptional facial recognition accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Autonomous Vehicle Safety and Efficiency Using Deep Learning and V2V Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The world is rapidly advancing towards automation, and one of the core evolutions in automation in the development of Autonomous Vehicles, have the potential to revolutionize the transportation field. However, they are not deemed as safe as manual driving. Moreover, current AVs rely on numerous expensive sensors, increasing cost and complexity. These sensors also introduce limitations like blind spots and vulnerability to manipulation. In addition to this, depending solely on on-board sensors and preprogramed algorithms can hinder decision-making and collaboration with other vehicles in complex situations. This paper presents a comprehensive study on impact of combined power of Deep Learning and vehicle-to-vehicle communication to enhance the safety and efficiency of AVs while utilizing a reduced sensor suite. Deep learning algorithms optimize the use of these sensors, improving perception and prediction capabilities, potentially reducing the need for additional sensors and their associated costs. V2V communication facilitates real-time information exchange, allowing AVs to share critical data such as location, speed, and intent with surrounding vehicles. This collaborative approach provides a more comprehensive understanding of the environment, leading to informed decision-making, it could reduce rear-end crashes by up to 80% and lane-change crashes by up to 50% as compared to traditional sensor-heavy AV systems.

articleTitle: Advanced U-Net++ Architecture for Precise Brain Tumor Segmentation in MRI Images: A Robust Solution for Medical Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Tumor segmentation in MRI images is a crucial process in medical imaging, aimed at accurately identifying and delineating tumor regions within the brain or other tissues. Hence proposed a modified U-Net++ based segmentation with predicted mask. To further improve the performance of the proposed method, incorporated additional layers into the U Net++ architecture. U-Net++ consists of Encoder Decoder and the encoder captures image content, while the decoder delineates object boundaries. U-Net++ excels in capturing both high-level and intricate details, which significantly boosts segmentation performance. This helps in accurate tumor segmentation of complex MRI images. To measure the effectiveness of the proposed model for segmentation and detection, Accuracy, Intersection over Union(IOU), Dice Coefficient and Area under the ROC Curve(AUC) scores are used. The proposed U-Net++ brought accuracy to 99 percent, which could significantly help in the process of accurate segmentation of human tissues. Accuracy of 39 % for IOU of 80, Dice Coefficient of $89 \%$, and $33 \%$ for the test set. This is equivalent to $8 \%$ sensitivity and accuracy and AUC of 78. The proposed method can be used as an additional diagnosis aid to help doctors determine the suitability of the treatment and the changes occurring in the body during the development of the disease

articleTitle: Security and Threats in Aviation: Cryptographic Based Network Security System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In present era, aviation communication technologies provides safe, effective, and efficient transfer of data between aircraft and facilities on the ground. Cryptography is essential to maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and legitimacy of data transfer in aviation systems. The safe key exchange and authentication that are essential components of aviation communication security are expertly ensured algorithms. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Rivest- Shamir- Adleman (RSA), Blowfish, Fernet, and Elliptic curve cryptog- raphy (ECC) are a few of the symmetric and asymmetric encryption method explored for aviation system. In this paper, the development and application of AES and Fernet encryption algorithms, specifically designed for safe client- server communication for the aviation industry sector, are the mainly implemented and performance analyzed. The public key is used for encryption, while the private key is used for decryption. The effectiveness of these algorithms in safeguarding data transfer between a client and server within an airline network is put to the test with great rigor.

articleTitle: Optimized Machine Learning Model for Alzheimer’s Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper presents an optimized machine learning model for Alzheimer’s disease classification, leveraging nature-inspired algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and Hunger Search Method (HSM). These algorithms are utilized to reduce data dimensionality while preserving crucial features, ensuring the integrity of the dataset. We then investigate the efficacy of neural network models, including Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and stacked ensemble models, in classifying Alzheimer’s disease. Our experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly enhances classification accuracy compared to conventional methods, offering a promising direction for improved diagnostic tools in Alzheimer’s research. Around 97% classification accuracy is obtained using stacked model with optimized features extracted using HSM.

articleTitle: CRLH-TL Based Compact Planar Dual Band Lowpass-Wide Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The compact dual band lowpass-wide bandpass filter (DB LWBF) proposed in this study is achieved utilising four Composite right/left-handed (CRLH) meandering shaped stubs (MSSs) connected to the main transmission line. In the lowpass band, the proposed filter has a measured -3 dB cut-off frequency of $1.09 ~\mathrm{GHz},~\left|S_{21}\right|$ better than 0.25 dB, and $\left|S_{11}\right|$ of less than 38 dB. The measured $\left|S_{21}\right|$ in the bandpass passband is 0.25 dB, with $\left|S_{11}\right|$ better than 28 dB and a fractional bandwidth of $79 \%$ at center frequency of 3.28 GHz. From 1.21 GHz to 1.57 GHz, the filter has greater than 17 dB stopband rejection level, and from 5.01 GHz to 7.25 GHz, it has a more than 20 dB stopband rejection level. For the proposed DB LWBF, electromagnetic simulations, Equivalent LC circuit representations, parametric analysis and measurement results are presented for the proposed DB LWBF. The proposed DB LWBF shows a small circuit size $\left(0.083 ~\lambda_{g} \times 0.048 ~\lambda_{g}\right)$, where $\lambda_{g}$ is the guided wavelength at 1.09 GHz), low insertion loss, wide out-of-band frequency range and high out-of-band rejection level.

articleTitle: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, and Digital Twins in Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Sustainable agriculture plays a key role in tackling worldwide food security issues and reducing environmental harm. Recent progress in the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Digital Twin technologies has demonstrated significant potential in transforming agricultural methods to be more sustainable. This study provides an in-depth analysis of how AI, IoT, and digital twins are being incorporated into sustainable agriculture, with a focus on their opportunities, obstacles, and future prospects. IoT sensors and devices play a significant role in enabling real-time data collection, analysis, and decision-making within agricultural operations. This capability allows for precise monitoring of crop growth, soil conditions, weather patterns, and resource usage, ultimately leading to optimized resource management and increased productivity while minimizing environmental impact. Additionally, digital twins, which are virtual representations of physical agricultural systems, provide opportunities for simulation, experimentation, and optimization of farming practices in a virtual setting. The article explores the diverse applications of IoT, AI, and digital twins in sustainable agriculture, such as precision farming, smart irrigation, pest and disease management, predictive analytics, and supply chain optimization. Through the examination of case studies, the paper showcases how these technologies effectively enhance crop yield, resource efficiency, and overall sustainability metrics.

articleTitle: The Age and Gender Detection using Deep Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Automatic age and gender classification has become important researcher since the rise of social platforms and social media. The main advancements in face recognition are the ability to determine a person's age and gender. This paper makes a significant contribution by providing a survey of different face recognition methods for determining age and gender. A deep neural network (DNN) known as a convolutional neural network is frequently used for natural language processing and image recognition and processing. The proposed method significantly enhances three elements: face alignment, face recognition, and face recognition accuracy. All weight vectors of people in the same age group within a given database are averaged together. To predict gender and age, picture classification and regression models have been discussed in this paper respectively. Although training the proposed network to make accurate predictions takes a lot of time, it significantly improves age and gender categorization precision. From the experimental results we compared and analyzed the work to the most recent UTK-Face benchmark for estimating age and gender.

articleTitle: PAPR Analysis of OTFS signal using Hyperbolic Tangent Companding Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: OTFS is one of the multi carrier modulation technique where the actual information will be stored in the delay Doppler domain. It provides superior performance than the OFDM when high Doppler’s present in the scenario and this is the current situation in the world, but it has large PAPR. To address this problem, in this work we incorporated simple known hyperbolic tangent comapnding technique. To know the effectiveness of the proposed companding, the simulations are drawn inview of various Scenarios. Simulations suggest that the HTC provides better performance than the $\mu$-law w.r.t to PAPR and BER as well.

articleTitle: IoT Based RFID Attendance System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Effective management of attendance systems is crucial for organizations seeking to streamline operations and enhance productivity. With the advent of technology, such as biometric attendance or RFID card-based systems, attendance management has become more advanced. Our proposed system, poised to provide smart attendance management by harnessing the combined power of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technologies, offers a promising solution to these challenges. This system automates attendance recording, where RFID cards assigned to individuals are seamlessly detected by RFID readers. The data is then transferred to a cloud-based server for central processing and storage, ensuring that attendance information is readily available and allowing administrators to remotely monitor and manage attendance operations. Additionally, our system notifies students immediately when their attendance is recorded.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Kintex-7 Low Voltage and Kintex UltraScale Technology for Advance Encryption Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This study compared the performance, power consumption, and resource utilization of two FPGA devices (Kintex-7 Low Voltage and Kintex UltraScale) for the AES encryption algorithm. The most significant difference was observed at the LVCMOS 12 where the Kintex UltraScale consumed 164.83% more power than he kintex-7 Low Voltage. The Kintex-7 Low Voltage utilized 50% more Slice LUTs and 93.28% more BUFGCTRL than Kintex UltraScale. The Kintex-7 Low Voltage FPGA is more power-efficient. At the same time, the Kintex UltraScale FPGA may be more suitable for applications that require specialized resource utilization, even if it consumes more power. The study emphasizes the importance of FPGA selection and I/O standards in enhancing power efficiency. It highlights the need to consider power consumption and resource utilization when selecting FPGA devices for complex algorithms like AES encryption.

articleTitle: Acquisition and Detection of Eye Movement Using Electrooculography
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) systems are becoming admired daily for eye-tracking environments. Electrooculography (EOG) is the technique for recording eye movement with the help of keeping electrodes near the eyes and forehead. EOG is captured by recording polarization potential between the cornea and retina, which measures corneal-retinal potential (CPR). In this concept, eye movement generates electric signals so that we can able to control the device in his/her environment and communicate with the required people. EOG signals are taken as the primary input using Electrodes. In the electrode first ionic energy converts into an electric signal in the body which is amplified and preprocessed to remove noise and artifacts then feature is extracted and used for real-time applications like biomedical and rehabilitation engineering applications, home automation, multitask gadget control, etc. In this process time domain features are calculated such as Mean, STD, RMS, Skewness, and Kurtosis then saccade and fixation are detected in Blink signal. In the future, EOGs may provide attractive means for virtual reality and valuable communication tools.

articleTitle: Implementation Challenges of AI for Agricultural Health Sustainability: An ISM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper investigates the implementation challenges that hinder the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) within the agricultural supply chain. By employing Interpretive Structural Modelling (ISM), a systematic technique of analyzing complicated interrelationships, the authors identify and analyze the key factors that significantly impact the successful implementation of AI in this domain. This approach sheds light on the relationships between these factors, providing valuable insights in the agricultural sector aiming to leverage AI for overall supply chain optimization.

articleTitle: Controlled Quantum Teleportation in Asymmetric Noisy Ambience
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Ideal Controlled quantum teleportation, discovered theoretically by Karlsson and Bourennane, is a weird paradigm of nonlocal transplantation of probability-amplitudes of an arbitrary unknown generic information-qubit possessed by a sender (Alice) on a qubit preserved by a distantly located receiver (Bob) under control or cooperation by a third party (Charlie) via maximally entangled Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state employed as the quantum channel with local operation and classical communication. The GHZ state is a fragile quantum resource and extremely sensitive to inevitable noisy environment causing decoherence. It fuels, therefore, an imperatively pressing demand to strategize a scheme for noise-resistant control quantum teleportation. We revisit the ideal control quantum teleportation but with a noisy Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger State in which each intertwining qubit suffers with differing noises and inequivalent levels, namely, bit-flip, amplitude-flip and phase-flip, i.e., asymmetric noise ambience. The controlling power, introduced by Li and Ghose, is invoked to assess the performance of the afore-described noisy strategy. It is seen that differing levels of noises breaks the classical bound of controlling power and, thereby, demonstrating the loosening authority of controller. Our findings suggest that to which extent of asymmetric noise ambience noisy control quantum teleportation is noise-tolerant.

articleTitle: Parallel-Connected Distribution Generation System Operating in Islanded Mode Using Improved Droop Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: To maintain dependable and effective operation, especially in islanded microgrid situations, integrating Distributed Generation (DG) units and renewable energy sources into electrical grids has required sophisticated control systems. In the present work a parallel connected DG integrates with solar PV, wind, and Ideal DC Voltage for an islanded microgrid with droop control technique has been proposed. This work used the improved droop control method for parallel-connected DG systems in islanded mode to ensure stable voltage and frequency of the system. The droop control technique, which has been around for a while in AC microgrid load sharing, has been improved to handle the issues of isolated network voltage and frequency stability. Droop coefficients are optimized as part of the proposed approach to improve dynamic responsiveness and reduce circulating currents between parallel inverters. The droop control technique controls voltage and frequency. A model of the proposed system has been modelled in MATLAB/ Simulink and results are verified under shifting load conditions and sources.

articleTitle: Facial Recognition based Attendance system using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Facial recognition technology plays a vital role in numerous industries in today’s digital era. It is a widely used biometric identification method for security, authentication, and identification purposes. Despite having lower accuracy rates compared to iris and fingerprint recognition, facial recognition is preferred due to its non-intrusive and touchless characteristics. Additionally, these systems are being more commonly integrated for attendance monitoring in schools, offices, and other establishments. The objective is to enhance attendance procedures by substituting labor-intensive and environmentally harmful manual methods. With the increasing need for effective attendance monitoring, the significance of facial recognition systems is on the rise.

articleTitle: Identification of Voltage Transients and Notches in a Distribution System Using True RMS and Naïve Bayes Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Frequent utilization of non-linear loads and power electronics devices (semiconductor devices) cause adverse power quality (PQ) disturbances due to this both utility and end users struggle for better power quality. Earlier diagnosis of PQ was time-consuming, currently, advanced monitoring devices and techniques are involved. In this paper, the Naïve Bayes Gaussian classifier and true RMS are discussed for the accurate identification of transients and notches. True RMS calculates the square of the instantaneousness value of input and then takes the averaging of signal and displays the square root of instantaneous value. True RMS perfectly monitors sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal waveforms. Using true RMS waveforms, feature extraction has been made for single-stage disturbances. Provided features further process with Naïve Bays Gaussian classifier. The Naïve Bayes algorithm assumes that one feature is independent of the occurrence of another by evaluating the mean and standard deviation for the training period of the set. The training has been performed on 40 data sets of each disturbance. The proposed artificial intelligence (AI) classifier provides $99.2 \%$ of testing accuracy in the identification of aforementioned disturbances. Thus, Naïve Bayes algorithm recommends adequately classifying single-stage notches and transients.

articleTitle: Asymmetric two-way Controlled Quantum Teleportation in Quantum Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Quantum teleportation with optimum quantum resources and hardware in a quantum network poses a pressing and demanding need. Here, we offer a protocol for asymmetric two-way controlled quantum teleportation via employing a sixteen-qubit entangled state as a resource in a quantum network consisting of five communicating participants Alice, Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and Eve. Our protocol is designed so that a sending party (Alice) transmit its three single information-qubits to three different parties Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> & Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, respectively and at the mean time, these three parties (Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> & Bob<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) send their Bell-like information-qubits back to the sender (Alice) under the supervision of administrator (Eve) by invoking projective Bell State measurements, GHZ-state measurements and X-basis measurements and local unitary operations. Furthermore, we have analyzed intrinsic efficiency of the protocol and compare our scheme with other competitive protocols.

articleTitle: PneumonXNet - A deep learning model for pneumonia detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Standard chest X-rays are used to diagnose pneumonia, an infection of the lungs that can be highly contagious due to being caused by viruses and bacteria. Nevertheless, this method is more time-consuming and routine-dependent with a bias in outcome. So to overcome these problem we developed PneumonXNet, a bespoke CNN model for the detection of pneumonia. We evaluated the performance of our method with respect to pre-trained models such as VGG16, EfficientNetB3 and ResNet50 on a X-ray image dataset comprising 5,856 images. The best result we have reached is a test accuracy of 97% with dropout value of 0.4 which is better than the pretrained models. The pre-trained model EfficientNetB3 showed the highest accuracy, which points on possible applications of transfer learning. This research signifies the capabilities of CNN models to streamline and improve detection on pneumonia, which in turn paves way for technological sophistication in health care sectors. The findings of this study carry significant impact on pneumonia detection, emphasizing the importance of deep learning model in pneumonia detection and how it can help in saving a lot of time for doctors and patients from the traditional X rays collecting systems. This can also reduce the overall treatment cost for patients. This research therefore offers new avenues for developing strong techniques for pneumonia identification, which hold promise for improving healthcare technology and patient outcomes in general.

articleTitle: An IoT Solution for Enhanced Tray Management Systems in Food Service and Industrial Settings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This study introduces TraySmart, a cutting-edge Internet of Things (IoT) tool meant to completely transform the effectiveness and administration of tray systems in industrial, food court, and cafeteria environments. TraySmart employs cutting-edge technologies like weight sensing, RFID tag reading, temperature monitoring, NFC for user interaction, and $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi} /$ Bluetooth for data transmission to tackle the widespread issues associated with tray management, such as inefficient operations, concerns about food safety, and less-than-ideal user experiences. The weight-sensing feature of the device makes it possible to identify objects on the tray and monitor the contents of the tray in real time. Reading RFID tags makes identifying and tracking items easier, improving inventory control and lowering loss. Food safety and quality assurance depend on food items maintaining their ideal temperatures, which is ensured via temperature monitoring. Furthermore, NFC technology enhances the eating experience by enabling users to engage with the smartphone for payments or feedback. The communication options on the device guarantee smooth data transfer to a central system, facilitating thorough data analysis and system optimization. This essay covers the creativity, design, and development of the TraySmart prototype, the difficulties faced, and the strategies used in the process. The report assesses TraySmart’s effect on operational efficiency, food safety standards, and customer happiness by carefully examining the outcomes of pilot testing. With its scalable solution to improve tray management systems, TraySmart marks a significant leap in the application of IoT technology in the food service and industrial sectors. The results highlight how IoT gadgets like TraySmart have the power to revolutionize operational procedures and service delivery, establishing a new benchmark for innovation in the industry.

articleTitle: Dynamic Speed Control of Axial Piston Pump Using Adaptive Model Predictive Control with Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: To facilitate velocity control of axial piston pump a mathematical model has been developed through Adaptive Model Predictive Control (MPC). Traditional control methods fail to deal with nonlinearities and dynamics of complex hydraulic systems. Robust control offered by adaptive MPC provides an optimised solution by continuously updating the system model and control parameters in real-time, with improved performance and stability. The result analysis indicates, the Adaptive Model Predictive Control (MPC) excels the Proportional-Integral (PI) controller in terms of rise time, settling time, percentage overshoot, and control effort for two different inputs. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in response time, accuracy, and robust control differs significantly from typical control approaches.

articleTitle: Improvement of Power Quality in Distribution Network at low voltage side by using DVR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The study investigated a power distribution system design featuring two feeder lines and a coupling bus tied to a single power supply. One of the feeder lines (Feeder Line 2) includes a Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) can inject the missing energy to a nonlinear load, Feeder Line 1, on the other hand, supplies power to a resistive load. The primary objective is to assess the impact of the DVR on both feeder lines under various disturbances like frequency deviations, voltage transients, voltage instability, and flickers. Key findings highlight “a Potential of the Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) to alleviate power quality issues, improving the load profile across the system. Additionally, a overall harmonic distortion or Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) values remained below a $5 \%$ threshold in all cases, except for voltage instability and flickers. This study emphasizes the role of customized power devices, such as DVRs, in improving power quality, especially in complex systems prone to disturbances.

Author Keywords: Instability in voltage and flickers in voltage. Dynamic voltage restorer (DVR)

articleTitle: A modeling and control of Load Frequency for Interconnected Thermal/Hydro/Nuclear Power System using PI and Fuzzy Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper present three area interconnected different power system frequency control using PI (Proportional Integral) and Fuzzy controller. This study focuses on a three-area system comprising a thermal power station in $1^{\text {st }}$ area, a hydro power plant in $2^{\text {nd }}$ area, and a nuclear power plant in $3^{\text {rd }}$ area. The usage of a proportional integrator (PI) and a FLC (Fuzzy logic controller) for load frequency adjustment in the Thermal, Hydro and Nuclear Power System is presented in the paper. The maximum allowed variation is $\pm 0.5 \mathrm{~Hz}$, and the frequency variation is highly undesirable. To investigate the performance of a three area system, we are comparing the overshoot and settling time values for each scenario using PI and fuzzy logic control techniques individually for $\mathbf{1 \%}$ distraction in either area. The findings demonstrate that the FLC has a short settling time to reach the ultimate steady state and insignificant peak overshoots. With MATLAB / SIMULINK software, the suggested controller’s efficacy is verified. The simulation results shows that the FLC effectively addresses the load frequency control issue.

articleTitle: IoT Based ECG Monitoring System for ICU
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper focuses on using a ECG sensor connected to IoT devices to monitor ECG signals in real-time, allowing for remote monitoring and analysis of heart activity. This can have numerous potential applications in the fields of health and medicine, making ECG monitoring more accessible and convenient. The objective of this paper is likely to develop a system that enables continuous and real-time ECG Signal monitoring using loT technology and a ECG sensor. The aim is to provide a convenient, accessible, and remote solution for ECG monitoring and potentially improve healthcare outcomes. In this paper, we demonstrate how to interface the AD8232 ECG sensor with an Arduino and visualize the ECG waveform using the Serial Plotter. Additionally, we will explore how to monitor the BIO graph online using any IT cloud platform. To achieve this, we will interface the AD8232 BIO sensor with an ESP32 and generate a BIO signal by attaching the sensor leads to the chest or hand. Using Ubidots parameters, such as the API Key or Token, we will send the BIO graph data to the cloud for real-time monitoring. This health monitoring system using technology aims to enhance healthcare quality by enabling the monitoring of health conditions, at home potentially minimizing the necessity for hospital trips. Through the integration of technology with bio sensors this initiative strives to play a role, in advancing telemedicine and tailored healthcare services.

articleTitle: GAN-Alz: Synthetic Data Generation for Multiclass Alzheimer’s Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Accurate detection of skin cancer, particularly melanoma, is crucial for effective treatment and patient survival. This study explores the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) enhanced by Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for skin cancer detection. CNNs have shown remarkable performance in image classification tasks but often require extensive labeled datasets, which are scarce in medical domains. To address this, GANs are employed to generate synthetic skin lesion images, augmenting the dataset and improving the model’s generalization capability. The proposed approach integrates a pre-trained CNN architecture fine-tuned with a combination of real and GANgenerated images, enhancing the network’s ability to distinguish between benign and malignant lesions. Experimental results demonstrate that the inclusion of GAN-augmented data improves the model’s accuracy by $7 \%$, achieving an overall accuracy of $94 \%$, with precision and recall rates of $92 \%$ and $93 \%$, respectively. These findings suggest that the GAN-augmented CNN model offers a promising solution for automated skin cancer screening

articleTitle: Automated Robot with UV-C Sterilizer for Disinfection of Public Places
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The novel coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19), has fundamentally altered our way of life and by means of how we connect with the outside world. The pandemic has made it imperative to develop practical disinfection techniques that may be used on a regular basis. It is highly necessary, especially at public places, to prevent the airborne and surface transmission of illnesses. Chemical disinfectants are used in most of the current approaches, which can be time-consuming and labor-intensive. Irradiation with ultraviolet (UV) light is a tried-and-true, effective disinfectant. Hospitals assisted living facilities, airports, and retail centers are among the public organizations that are becoming more interested in using UV disinfection robots. In this present paper the glimpse of a functional UV-C Sterilizer Robot shall be provided.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Engineering Placement Outcomes Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: It is difficult to predict where engineering graduates will be employed due to various factors including market needs, technical skills, personal qualities, and academic achievement. Traditional techniques often produce less-than-ideal results because they are unable to fully capture the complex interactions between these factors. In this paper, we provide a novel method to tackle this problem by using genetic algorithm (GA) placement prediction capabilities. Genetic algorithms mimic the principles of evolution to find optimal solutions in a large solution space. The process of natural selection inspires them. GA effectively searches the solution space by listing possible solutions as chromosomes and performing selection, crossover, and mutation operations to identify optimal solutions.

articleTitle: Prediction of Share Price by Using Machine Learning Algorithm: Multiple Linear Regression Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to predict the Year End Share Price of Australian Mining Companies. This study investigates the relationship between the various financial metrics and the year-end share price of companies experiencing financial distress. Key metrics such as ‘ BV per Share (${\$}$)’, ‘Enterprise Value (${\$}$)’, ‘Gross CF per Share (${\$}$)’, ‘Cash per Share (${\$}$)’, ‘Sales per Share (${\$}$)’, ‘ROE’, ‘Financial Leverage’, ‘Asset Turnover’, ‘ROA’ are analyzed. The dataset includes [395rows $\times$ 33columns] observations, [Mean Squared Error: 0.38, R-square: 0.90] in Linear Regression and [Mean Squared Error: 0.34, R-square: 0.91] in XG Boost the model achieved an R-squared value of 0.91, indicating high predictive accuracy. The results highlight XG Boost’s efficiency in precisely predicting share prices and have implications for financial decision-making and investment strategies in unpredictable markets.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Application Based Linear-Nonlinear loads
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper comprehensively analyzes linear and nonlinear loads across residential, commercial, and industrial sectors. Linear loads draw sinusoidal currents, while nonlinear loads like power electronics draw distorted currents, injecting harmonics into the power system. The proliferation of nonlinear loads has led to power quality issues such as voltage distortion.MATLAB/Simulink simulations demonstrate the effects of nonlinear loads on voltage and current waveforms. Innovative mitigation strategies, from traditional filtering to AI-powered control systems, are explored for managing harmonics and ensuring grid stability. Recommendations are made for effectively managing linear and nonlinear loads to maintain power quality and grid stability. Embracing the challenges posed by nonlinear loads and developing robust solutions is crucial for a resilient modern power grid. The future of power systems lies in harnessing advanced technologies and control strategies to mitigate the impact of nonlinear loads while optimizing efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Lung Cancer Detection Using CNN, KNN, and SVM Algorithms: Evaluating Accuracy and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of mortality, emphasizing the crucial need for early detection to improve survival rates. Computed tomography (CT) imaging stands out as a pivotal strategy in this endeavor. However, the escalating volume of CT images necessitates efficient and accurate automated detection methods to mitigate manual labeling efforts and ensure consistent results. This research paper employs a comprehensive strategy, merging traditional machine learning models (including KNN and SVM) with state-of-the-art feature extraction methods such as PCA, HOG, and VGG16 transfer learning, as well as utilizing a dedicated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for classification. By amalgamating these methodologies, the study seeks to comprehensively evaluate their efficacy in accurately diagnosing lung cancer. The anticipated outcomes aim to contribute novel insights to medical image analysis, particularly in advancing early cancer detection. Through this research, valuable contributions are expected to be made towards the enhancement of medical image analysis techniques, thereby pushing the boundaries of early cancer detection and ultimately improving patient outcomes. The best result of the proposed model shows the accuracy percentage of the SVM classifier varies from ${9 0 \%}$ to ${9 6 \%}$, the accuracy of the KNN classifier varies from 95% to 100%, and the accuracy of the CNN classifier varies from ${9 6 \%}$ to ${9 9 \%}$.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Electric Drive Mechanism for Lifting the Shutter of a drainage dam using Programmable Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In this paper the design and installation of a water level control system based on PLCs is the main work. Numerous water-saving systems are in place to deliver water from the dam (A wall that holds back water). Thus, it is crucial to open and close the dam gate in order to conserve water. The proposed system achieved a shutter opening/closing time of 10 seconds. Additionally, the PLC-based controller exhibited a response time of ${1 0}$ milliseconds to control signals, ensuring rapid and efficient shutter movement. The goal of the dam automation system with a PLC (programming logic controller) base is to control the water level in the dam reservoir area. Dam gates are controlled by both manual and programmable logic controller (PLC) systems. The PLC is used to regulate the releasing and shutting of dam gates in order to save water resources for irrigation and to operate the dam gate efficiently based on the water level. It also aids in warning nearby residents about impending flooding. A collection of level sensors, a PLC, relays, and a DC motor make up this system. A series of level sensors are used to measure the water level and provide an input signal to a PLC. PLC uses data from level sensors to manage the dam’s gate. To open and close the gate, a dc motor is driven by relays in both forward and backward directions. This autonomous system’s operation will be entirely dependent on the PLC’s ladder diagram programming technique.

articleTitle: Loan Approval Prediction Based on Tabu Search Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The banks and their customers know loan approval methods. Although traditional methods like taking all the relevant information are time-consuming, there is a need for technology, which can result in machine learning algorithms being applied to the data sets that contain the past data of customers to help in predicting whether the loan is being approved or not. Now the question is how much these algorithms predict accurate results, our research paper tells how the optimization we applied will maximize the number of loan approvals and minimize the risk analysis. We applied the Tabu search optimization along with a few machine-learning algorithms on the loan data set, and our accuracy is about ${9 8 \%}$.

articleTitle: Method for Detecting Potato Leaf Disease Using the YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Potato leaf diseases pose a significant risk to the global potato sector, with significant financial implications. It is vital to precisely and efficiently target agricultural productivity and disease management. This work presents the YOLOv8 deep learning model as a method for recognizing and categorizing diseases in potato leaves. The proposed methodology effectively uses YOLOv8’s high detection precision to detect and classify illnesses affecting potato leaves. Many images were used to help the model’s training process, including healthy and sick potato leaves. The test results revealed that the proposed methodology correctly discovered and classified leaf disease in potato plants with a 98.6 % accuracy. This technique has the potential to significantly improve the quality and productivity of potato crops in precision agriculture systems by detecting diseases early on and adopting control measures. The experimental results support the proposed framework’s operational capability, which has great promise for reliably detecting and predicting potato crop illnesses.

articleTitle: Design, Utilization, and Performance Enhancement of Instrumentation Amplifiers in Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Instrumentation amplifiers (InAmps) play a crucial role in biomedical instrumentation by amplifying small differential signals while attenuating common-mode noise. This research paper focuses on the design utilization and performance optimization of InAmps for biomedical applications. Key aspects explored include noise reduction, common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR), and power efficiency. Simulations conducted using MATLAB Simulink demonstrate that chopper stabilization significantly reduces low-frequency noise, improving the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by approximately 15 dB. Utilizing low-noise operational amplifiers decreases input-referred noise by 30%, enhancing signal clarity. Precision resistor matching improves CMRR by 20 dB, while balanced layouts contribute an additional 10 dB improvement by minimizing electromagnetic interference. Operating amplifiers at lower supply voltages reduces power consumption by 40%, with a 25% reduction achieved through careful component selection. These findings offer valuable insights into designing robust and efficient instrumentation amplifiers for various biomedical applications, paving the way for advancements in portable and reliable health monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Topic Modeling and EDA for Analyzing User Sentiments for ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper uses Topic Modeling and Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Twitter data to investigate user emotions on ChatGPT. We find recurring themes and patterns in user thoughts by analyzing millions of tweets. While EDA investigates temporal trends, user demographics, and general sentiment landscapes, we leverage topic modeling, namely Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), to discover important discussion topics. Through the integration of Topic Modeling and EDA, the research offers a comprehensive perspective on user sentiments and insights into the perceptions of ChatGPT on Twitter. Sentiment analysis, performed using VADER and Twitter-roBERTa, shows that 65% of tweets were positive, 25% neutral, and 10% negative. VADER and roBERTa differ significantly in sentiment classification, with roBERTa identifying 12% more negative sentiments. This integrated approach provides a comprehensive view of user sentiments and highlights areas of concern, such as potential misuse and reliability. The findings contribute to the ongoing discourse on AI usage and suggest the need for further research across different platforms and over extended periods to capture evolving sentiments and inform the development of AI technologies.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Solar Irradiance using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In modern power system application the forecasting of incident solar irradiance plays very important role for energy management optimally for operation the power grid efficiently. To forecast the output power of solar Photo Voltaic based electricity generation system the prediction of solar irradiance is very helpful. This forecast of solar irradiance is conducted by different techniques under physical models based strategy combined to cloud imagery and algorithm based approach using machine learning (ML) methods to develop prediction models associated with artificial intelligence (AI). This article is giving details of the implementation and execution of a strategy for solar irradiation forecasting developed using ML. Results analysis using proposed method is compared among ML based methodologies on regression model, decision tree, boosting and bagging for performing solar irradiance prediction applications. The performance measurements are challenging due to complexity of data set diversity, forecasting horizon, time step, performance indicators, and setup. The Linear regression gave minimum RMSE, MSE and prediction speed as $0.80359,0.64575$ and 21000 observations per second. Lowest MAE and training time is obtained for decision tree as 0.58321 and 5.3601 sec. The results presented here are highly efficient and helps to improve prediction performance by minimizing error and enhancing speed by the proposed novel approach.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Real-Time Noise Removal in Retinal Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Real-time noise removal in fundus images, which are images of the back of the eye (retina), is a critical task in various medical applications, particularly in ophthalmology. This study presents a deep learning approach for denoising retinal fundus images affected by gaussian and speckle noise. A diverse dataset comprising various retinal image acquisition conditions was utilized, with synthetic speckle and gaussian noise introduced at different levels to simulate in real-world scenarios. In the proposed approach, the noise is introduced by considering the variance of 0.5 and 1. Moreover, pre-processing steps were employed to mitigate noise impact, followed by feeding the images into a proposed CNN-based denoising architecture. The architecture’s performance was rigorously evaluated using quantitative metrics and expert clinician assessments. Results include an average Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 47.5 dB, an average Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.90, and an average $R 2$ score of $71 \pm 0.7 \%$. Additionally, the BRISQUE score averaged 59.41. These results demonstrate the efficacy of the approach in enhancing image quality and preserving essential features, highlighting its potential for clinical applications in retinal imaging.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Multinomial Naïve Bayes and XG Boost for Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Social-media provides a vast amount of user-generated content which serves as an invaluable source of real-time data for analyzing public sentiments about various aspects. Public sentiment shapes various services and strategies as per the targeted users. Analyzing text for sentiments or opinions comes under a branch of Natural language processing (NLP), known as Sentiment analysis. Various approaches have been used for sentiment analysis from time to time, viz., machine learning methods, lexicon-based approaches and hybrid of these approaches. This paper uses machine leaning methodologies for sentiment analysis. It explores the effectiveness of Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB) and Gradient boosting using XG Boost in sentiment analysis. The strength and limitations of both approaches are explored using cross-validation technique. This approach contributes to existing research in the area of sentiment investigation by critically assessing the performance of proposed model and by providing valuable implications in the areas like brand monitoring and public opinion.

articleTitle: Review Paper of Metal Insulator Metal and Metal Oxide Metal Capacitors for Improved Capacitance and Overall Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This review distinguishes the working principles, fabrication techniques, and various parameters such as capacitance values, voltages, fabrication cost, area, capacitance density, and leakage currents of metal-oxide-metal (MOM) and metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors. These days, because of their benefits and affordability, these capacitors are utilized in chip design. MOM capacitors are manufactured and frequently interdigitated with metal contacts. MIM capacitors are constructed differently than other capacitors since they are mostly made of distinct metal layers separated by a dielectric layer. The cost of MIM capacitors is more than MOM capacitors but MOM capacitors are mostly limited to use. By comparing, we showed that the two capacitors’ performances were similar in the preliminary analysis, suggesting that MOM capacitors might eventually partially replace MIM capacitors in semiconductor production.

articleTitle: Analysis of Symmetric Cryptographical Algorithms in Real Time File Transfer Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Since the dawn of internet software growth, we have resided in a digital environment fraught with cybersecurity concerns. The sophistication in today’s traditional security measures is one of the primary reasons for the increasing number of cyberattacks, thus leaking sensitive data. Encryption, which involves transforming plain text into cipher text, is important for maintaining software security and preventing the unauthorized entry of probable hackers. However, it is evident that the encryption algorithms generally have a high resource requirement in terms of memory, processing time, and electricity. This paper compares ten more common used encryption algorithms: AES, Blowfish, CAST5, Camellia, ChaCha20, DES, 3DES, RC2, SEED, and SM4. There have been evaluations under different conditions: different data types and sizes and requirements for CPU time and encryption/decryption speed. The results of these simulations have pinpointed that each of the algorithms is good enough on its own to be efficient and effective, hence helping the organizations choose the more appropriate technique for their software’s security. Therefore, this work importantly contributes to the field of cybersecurity as it adds posing of extensive examination on the most represented encryption algorithms and their performances in different situations. Organizations use the stringent encryption methods to secure their software and data which lessens the odds of cyberattack and data leak.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis of different cloud computing method for scheduling healthcare tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The problem of efficient task scheduling in cloud-integrated, Internet of Things-based healthcare monitoring systems is examined in this work. We suggest Prioritized Sorted Task-Based Allocation (PSTBA), a novel scheduling method, to enhance task execution and boost system performance. In order to guarantee that vital healthcare monitoring tasks are finished on time, PSTBA ranks jobs according to their criticality, expected processing time (EPT), and virtual machine wait time. The process entails putting PSTBA into practice in an IoT cloud context and assessing its effectiveness using in-depth CloudSim simulations. The findings show that PSTBA works noticeably better than the current techniques, such as First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) and Sorted Task-Based Allocation (STBA) PSTBA specifically lowers the failure rate by 20% and 35.6%, raises the guarantee ratio by 2.5% and 4.8%, and decreases latency by 12.6% compared to STBA and 79.2% compared to FCFS. Moreover, PSTBA successfully reduces the number of key activities missed by 14.9% when compared to STBA and 51% when compared to FCFS. To sum up, PSTBA is a very successful scheduling method that improves job prioritizing and system stability for IoT-based healthcare systems.

articleTitle: A Transfer Learning Approach for Enhancing Road Surface Classification in Intelligent Driving Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Road surface classification is very critical in the domain of intelligent driving systems as it ensures enhanced safety and comfort in autonomous vehicles. In this paper, a transfer learning approach is proposed for effectively classifying the road surface with enhanced accuracy and real-time performance mitigating the constraints of traditional image processing techniques A deep learning model is developed and trained in this research using an open-source dataset, encompassing 72,400 images capturing distinct road surface characteristics present across varying terrains. This research adopts pre-trained models like Mobilenet, VGG-19 and Resnet101 as feature extractors to optimize and improve the classification performance of the deep learning model significantly. The proposed methodology is evaluated using different key performance metrics such as loss, accuracy, average rate of improvement and change in accuracy, and total training time. The proposed deep learning technique achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 7 7 \%}$, signifying its critical importance for real-world applications and practical deployment.

articleTitle: All Optical 3-To-8 Line Decoder Device Design Using 2D Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the development of an all-optical communication network to achieve terabit per second bit rates, an essential requirement for future high-speed data transmission. Unlike conventional networks that rely on electronic components, an all-optical network utilizes photonic devices exclusively for data transmission, reception, and processing, leveraging two-dimensional photonic crystals (2DPhCs) for their superior performance and ease of fabrication compared to three-dimensional counterparts. 2DPhCs exhibit perfect photonic band gaps, making them ideal for creating various optical components such as routers, demultiplexers, decoders, and switches essential for an all-optical network.Recent advancements include the design of alloptical decoders, crucial for signal processing within these networks. Notably, decoders incorporating nonlinearity in the PhC platform have been explored, revealing significant findings on refractive phenomena and beam propagation at the PhC interface. Challenges remain, such as the high power requirements and limited data rates of existing designs. This paper delves into the evolution and optimization of 2DPhC-based optical decoders, with a focus on performance enhancement through design modifications. Studies have demonstrated improvements in signal-to-noise ratio, power efficiency, and decoding precision by adjusting parameters like defect size and lattice constant. Future directions point towards integrating additional functionalities and achieving dynamic reconfigurability in all-optical decoders, which are critical for the next-generation photonic integrated circuits (PICs). Through this comprehensive examination, the report aims to underscore the potential of 2DPhCs in revolutionizing all-optical communication networks and guiding future research towards more efficient and versatile optical devices.

articleTitle: Controlling Mouse Cursor through Eye Movement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Within the past few years, there have been significant advancements in the computer and human interaction. Earlier, keyboard and mouse were the primary input method, then touch screen came in the existence and now many other technologies are being used to provide input to the computer. In the advancement of technological process this research paper presents an iris movement-based mouse cursor control systems that allows users to control the computer cursor using their eye movements. The proposed system aims to improve computer interaction by integrating advanced computer vision and gaze detection techniques especially for those who face difficulties with traditional input methods due to physical disabilities. The objective is to enhance the efficiency, reliability, and accuracy of iris movement-based cursor control system.
