The implementation of this system has several key stages, including video processing, iris tracking, cursor control, and user interaction. The proposed system stimulates mouse movement and click events based on eye movement and gaze patterns, and provides an environment for interaction. This proposed system is tested on various parameters like increased frame rate, low lighting, background effects, etc. The performance of the system is measured in terms of correct position trials and it is $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$ for the proposed system.

articleTitle: Solar Grass Cutter Technology based Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper introduces a solar-powered grass cutter employing Internet of Things (IoT) technology for remote control through the Blynk application. The system integrates components like Arduino UNO, solar panel, DC motor, motor driver, rechargeable batteries, and a WiFi module. Programmed via Arduino IDE, the grass cutter features functions such as forward, backward, right, left, on, off, and stop. Additionally, a hand gesture-controlled version is explored, enabling obstacle-free operation from any direction. The system utilizes batteries for motor and cutter functions, charged by solar panels, eliminating the need for extra batteries. The IoT-based approach enables control through a smartphone, promoting efficiency and environmentally sustainable grass cutting. IoT-based solar-powered grass cutter effectively tackles the environmental issues associated with traditional grass cutting methods. By harnessing renewable energy, incorporating intelligent technology for automation and remote control, and ensuring minimal emissions and noise, these cutting-edge machines emerge as a prominent and sustainable solution for maintaining green spaces in diverse settings.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in Backscatter NOMA Network with Optimum Throughput
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: One of the strongest growth area in telecommunication is wireless services. This growth is due to the rise in connectivity, customer centricity, automation, connected devices, artificial intelligence etc. In wireless communication, to improve the capacity of networks a new technique of Non Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is thoroughly used. The combination of NOMA and backscatter communication (BackCom) provides many new probabilities for vast connectivity that in turn used to enhance the range of network. Wireless networks confer several challenges. One main challenge is the performance destruction of backscatter communication in multiple cell network of NOMA under the consequence of interference. To overcome this problem, a suitable technique of resource allocation is proposed. In this paper, a single cell model of resource allocation is presented. To get the optimum throughput proportional fair scheduling technique is used.

articleTitle: Quantum Tele-Amplification of Non-Gaussian State via bi-modal Asymmetric Entangled Coherent State
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Optical Coherent State (OCS), generated by LASERS, exhibits Gaussian probability (Wigner) distribution function with minimum uncertainty-spread in quantum phase space. It provides over-complete states spanning infinite dimensional Hilbert space, an emblematic instance of continuous variable states. Quantum superposition of Cat Coherent States (CCS), named as Schrodinger CCS due to historical reasons and visualized as non-Gaussian Wigner distribution function in phase space, furnishes quantum resources for quantum information science, engineering and technology i.e., quantum non-locality, quantum teleportation, and tele-amplification, to name a few. We proposed a protocol to teleporting mono-modal non-Gaussian OCS (Schrodinger CCS) conjoined with its amplification via asymmetric two mode entangled CCS as quantum channel. The fidelity and probability of successful event and unsuccessful event quantum tele-amplification is defined for various heralding conditions at sender’s lab. It is seen that the probability of faithful and unfaithful quantum tele-amplification is fifty percent with unit fidelity for intense OCS. Prospective utility of our scheme may overlong distances transmission where loss in photon is inevitable.

articleTitle: Predicting Steel Fatigue Using Machine Learning Techniques for sustainable Infrastructure Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Ensuring the structural integrity of steel infrastructure is crucial for sustainable development. Fatigue damage, a major concern in steel structures, can lead to catastrophic failures. This paper investigates the application of machine learning (ML) techniques for predicting steel fatigue life. The work compares the performance of eight regression models using a publicly available dataset MatNavi from the National Institute for Material Science (NIMS). The model performance is evaluated using three metrics: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared Score. The results show that Gradient Boosting achieves the lowest error metrics, demonstrating superior performance in predicting fatigue life. Random Forest also exhibits high accuracy, suggesting its potential as an alternative method. While Huber Regressor shows higher error values, its potential for handling outliers might be valuable in specific scenarios. This study highlights the effectiveness of machine learning, particularly ensemble methods, for predicting steel fatigue and emphasizes their potential in enhancing sustainable infrastructure management.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Optimizing Smart Cities Traffic Flow for the Carbon Emission Control Through Modern Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This research study describes a pioneering program in Chandigarh aiming at reducing carbon emissions and optimizing traffic flow by combining Scalable Urban Traffic Control with Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication technology. The study explores how these contemporary technologies can be included into the infrastructure of the city’s traffic management system, emphasizing how they can greatly lessen traffic and lessen their impact on the environment. The suggested strategy aims to improve traffic signal system efficiency and enable dynamic routing through real-time data analysis and adaptive control mechanisms. The effectiveness of this creative solution is demonstrated through case studies and simulations, providing insightful information for decision-makers and urban planners who are tackling the difficulties of contemporary urban mobility. Following the implementation of Scalable Urban Traffic Control with Vehicle-to-Infrastructure in Chandigarh city, there was a discernible reduction in carbon monoxide levels

articleTitle: Systematic Exploration of GAN-Generated Image Recognition Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Nowadays, GANs are becoming more and more skilled at producing realistic imagery. Furthermore, as GAN technologies continue to progress, reliable and transparent detection techniques must be created in order to protect digital content integrity and uphold public confidence. Hence, it is of utmost importance to enhance the recognition ability of deep learning models to discriminate between actual and GAN-generated images. The widespread use of GAN images raises ethical concerns regarding deep fake’s proliferation and cyber security risks. The methods for identifying images produced by Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are thoroughly examined in this research accompanied by their practical applications. Using GAN-generated images as a backdrop, the paper reviews current image recognition methods. Key factors for successful GAN image recognition are highlighted in this review by addressing the significance and challenges of identifying GAN-generated images, which also evaluates the advantages and disadvantages of various techniques. The article also delves into the societal and ethical implications by outlining potential future directions and areas for investigation in the rapidly developing fields of image recognition and GAN technology.

articleTitle: Designing of Home Automation based DTMF Using GSM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a DTMFbased home automation system using GSM technology. The proposed system leverages Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF) signaling and Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) to enable remote control of home appliances. The system architecture consists of an Arduino Uno microcontroller, a DTMF decoder, a GSM module, and relays. The DTMF tones generated by pressing keys on a mobile phone are decoded and used to control the relays connected to home devices. This approach allows for reliable and cost-effective remote operation of appliances, even in areas with limited internet connectivity. The results demonstrate the effectiveness, reliability, and accessibility of the DTMF-based home automation system, making it a promising solution for smart home applications. The key findings are Reliable DTMF-based communication and control, even with limited internet connectivity, through the use of a GSM module. Cost-effective implementation using readily available and low-cost components, making the system accessible to a wider user base. Scalable and modular design that allows easy expansion to accommodate additional home devices. Improved accessibility and user-friendliness, particularly for physically challenged individuals, through the mobile app interface and DTMF-based control.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of All Optical Adders for Next Generation Processors Using 2D Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This project explores the development of an all-optical address system for next-generation processors through the utilization of 2D photonic crystals. The objective is to enhance processing speed and efficiency by replacing traditional electronic addressing with optical counterparts. The design involves intricate analysis of the 2D photonic crystal structures to optimize performance. The study tries to show the viability and benefits of this novel strategy through simulation and experimentation. The potential benefits include reduced signal latency, lower power consumption, and increased data transfer rates. The research contributes to the advancement of optical computing paradigms, addressing the challenges in contemporary processor architectures.

articleTitle: Architectural Design for AdhaarAssist — A Forward-Looking Lock-Free STM Solution for Adhaar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Any parallel program is judged based on its efficiency in doing multiple tasks at the same time without getting stuck due to an underlying problem. The main purpose of a parallel program is to effectively and quickly solve a large and complicated problem at hand. This is why; parallel programs form the basis of many powerful supercomputers where parallel computing is supported through special hardware which is complemented with parallel software achieving hundreds of petaflop/s of performance. The biggest challenge for a parallel programmer is to build a program that has a minimum tradeoff for increased parallelism and good concurrency control among the parallel tasks. One of the biggest applications of parallelism is the huge, ever-increasing database of Adhaar biometric. Its crucial to have a robust, fast and efficient way of accessing and manipulating this data so that along with faster results, consistency of the database is also maintained. This paper proposes a schema AdhaarAssist which is a lock-free STM based algorithm that will work on a shared in-memory data structure. Some of its features are increased concurrency by lazy conflict detection, partial aborts that optimize the algorithm for maximum throughput when complex and lengthy transactions are employed, memory barriers and timestamping. The algorithm proposed in this paper will open the way for leveraging it for distributed-shared in-memory databases like the one used by Adhaar.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning for Effective Customer Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: The paper’s objective is to utilize machine learning techniques for customer segmentation. We aim to identify significant patterns and segments within a customer base to enhance marketing strategies, improve customer satisfaction, and optimize business operations. By mastering Python programming alongside essential libraries like Pandas, NumPy, and data visualization tools, we focus on data collection, training, and testing to construct a robust customer segmentation model. Such a model will enable businesses to enhance their marketing strategies, customer satisfaction, and streamline operations. This paper delves into customer segmentation using k-means clustering, analysing the Mall Customers dataset to demonstrate how machine learning can effectively segment customers created on their purchasing behaviour and demographic information. The study includes an extensive review of literature, detailed research methodology, implementation of the clustering algorithm, evaluation of models, and discussion of the results. The model’s accuracy is verified using two metrics: the Silhouette score, which is 0.69777, and the Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI), which is ${0. 4 2 1 1 0}$.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Automatic Sanitization Solution for Human Being in Real World Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: During climax of COVID-19, research revealed that the virus primarily spreads through close contact with respiratory droplets from infected people and by touching surfaces that have been contaminated. To curb the transmission of this virus and similar viral infections, healthcare experts advised frequent cleaning and disinfecting practices. This paper proposes a contactless sanitization system designed to enhance human safety. The system incorporates various features, including height detection, body temperature checks, and sanitization capabilities, to minimize the risk of contamination. Additionally, it is designed to be accessible to individuals with disabilities, such as those with hearing or visual impairments. By addressing these needs, the system aims to provide a comprehensive solution for reducing the spread of infections while ensuring inclusivity for all users. This approach not only focuses on preventing disease transmission but also emphasizes the importance of accessibility and user-friendliness in public health measures.

articleTitle: Modelling, Design and Control of PV-Wind-Battery Hybrid Power System using MPPT Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: In this research, we have introduced a hybrid power model that combine the unique characteristics of wind turbines and solar panels to generate electrical power and supply it to a grid station. Two control strategies have been implemented to maximize power point tracking in both the solar & wind turbine circuits. Furthermore, a voltage source converter is employed on the grid side to change DC - AC using the second control technique. The viability of the system is demonstrated through comprehensive simulation results, accompanied by a detailed description of the complete hybrid system. The software simulation model is developed with Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Grid Connected PV Array and Battery Energy Storage Interface EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper represents an effective design approach that makes use of a charging station with maximum power point tracking and a DC-DC converter with Energy Storage Unit. On the other hand, surplus solar energy is fed into the electrical grid. ESU (energy storage unit) uses the stored energy to produce the finest power management system presented. Consequently, an off-grid EV charging station that is reliable, efficient, and kind to the environment is produced. This paper also highlights several key findings. The integration of PV arrays with battery storage enhances the reliability and efficiency of EV charging, reducing grid dependency by approximately $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$. The system’s energy utilization efficiency was improved by $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$ due to optimized power management strategies. Furthermore, the setup demonstrated a potential reduction in peak demand charges by up to 15%, contributing to cost savings and grid stability.

articleTitle: Migration RoadMap for On-Premises ERP To Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This research study describes the complexity and the aspects associated with the process of migration of the on-premise Enterprise Resource Planning systems to the cloud-based ones. Enterprises are much more aware nowadays of the benefits of cloud ERPs in terms of scalability, flexibility, and affordability that are enforcing them to exist in the dynamic environment of business. However, a number of challenges still prevail toward the successful migration process regarding data migration, application simplification, infrastructural issues, and perfect change management. This paper synthesizes the insight from the different stakeholders—senior leadership teams, operations managers, financial specialists, and IT professionals—to give in-depth perceptivity on the journey of migration. The research adds some pragmatic recommendations and industry best practices to help businesses overcome ERP conversion initiatives, based on analyses of various goals and different viewpoints held by co-stakeholders. This research emphasizes stakeholder participation, strategic planning in the face of uncertainty, and systemic framework as important means to help overcome unexpected roadblocks. This paper aims to equip businesses with information and resources to negotiate all complexities in moving their ERPs successfully to the cloud, thus helping them exploit the full power brought about by cloud-based solutions while reducing the risks and challenges that accompany the change.

articleTitle: Discerning and Leveraging Gastric Cancer Using Deep Analytics Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Gastric disease (GC) is one of the most prevalent malignant developments with poor prognostic outcomes. Endoscopic evaluation is primarily used for early recognition, while pathological confirmation and CT scanning are used for further treatment. The shortage of pathologists presents an opportunity for AI systems to ease the workload and increase diagnostic accuracy. Most gastric cancers show genetic instability, either microsatellite or chromosomal, which occurs early in carcinogenesis. New classifications based on histologic features, genotypes, and molecular profiles improve understanding, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of each subtype. This paper introduces “Gastronet,” a deep learning system integrating three algorithms—Perform Multiple Tasks Net, Mix Net, and Overall Net—to enhance gastric cancer diagnosis. Gastronet aims to provide precise predictions with minimal additional confirmation, surpassing current diagnostic models. The roadmap includes a comprehensive literature review to identify gaps in current diagnostic methods and the potential for AI, followed by the development of Perform Multiple Tasks Net, Mix Net, and Overall Net to handle specific diagnostic tasks and data types. Data collection and preprocessing ensure a quality dataset for training and validation. Each network is trained and validated separately, then integrated and fine-tuned within the Gastronet framework. The system’s performance is compared with current models, demonstrating superior accuracy. Implementation involves developing a user-friendly interface for clinical use and integrating it into workflows. Continuous improvement is ensured by updating the system with new data and advancements in gastric cancer research. By following this roadmap, the paper aims to develop a reliable, accurate, and efficient system for early detection and diagnosis of gastric cancer, improving patient outcomes and supporting pathologists.

articleTitle: Soliciting the Problem of Manual Scavenging Using Advanced Robot Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Manual scavenging is a degrading and unethical practice that violates human rights and perpetuates social disparities. Despite being prohibited in India since 1993, it continues due to the social and economic disadvantage of the Dalit minority, who are primarily hired as manual scavengers. This essay explores the potential use of modern robotics technology to eradicate manual scavenging and improve social equity. The study examines the challenges and limitations of transitioning from manual scavenging to robotics technology, including the displacement of manual scavengers and the need for rehabilitation and reintegration. Advanced robotics technologies, such as robotic excreta cleaning systems, could replace manual scavenging and promote social fairness. However, adopting these technologies for manual scavenging requires a thorough understanding of the social and economic causes and systemic adjustments. The project aims to integrate advanced robotics technology with legal changes and social interventions to improve social equity and eradicate manual scavenging. This research paper result contributes to the ongoing discourse on manual scavenging by emphasizing the potential of modern robotics technology to enhance social justice and eradicate this inhumane practice.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Techniques for Accurate Heart Disease Detection: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Globally, heart disease poses a significant challenge to public health. Early identification is crucial for effectively managing and treating heart conditions. Machine learning has shown promising results in predicting medical problems for the past few years. In this study, A system was developed that is capable of detecting cardiovascular diseases using machine learning methods. The project consists of Data loading, Exploratory data analysis, preprocessing, training, evaluation and storage. A dataset was introduced that contained an array of characteristics related to the cardiovascular health status (such as age, gender, cholesterol level.). However, training measured the accuracy of 3 algorithms: K Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Decision Tree, and Random Forest in identifying heart ailment. The article also returns an ensemble graph that considers the forecasts of both these models together, saving the best GNB model for future use. Results showed that the machine learning methods are proficient in heart problem identification, as in this hybrid model, with a 97.32% accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Enhancing CNN Classification with Lamarckian Memetic Algorithms and Local Search
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Optimization is critical for achieving optimal performance in deep neural networks (DNNs). Traditional gradient-based methods, such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and ADAM, often face challenges like local minima entrapment and slow convergence rates. This paper explores population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithms for image classification networks. We propose a novel approach integrating a two-stage training technique with population-based optimization algorithms and local search capabilities to enhance solution quality and convergence speed. In the first stage, a global search is conducted using a population-based algorithm to explore the solution space extensively, allowing the network to escape local minima and find promising regions. In the second stage, a local search fine-tunes the solutions from the global search, ensuring improved accuracy and stability. Our experiments show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art gradient-based techniques like ADAM in accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios with high computational complexity and numerous trainable parameters. The results suggest that our approach offers a robust and efficient alternative for weight optimization in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Future work will explore integrating adaptive mechanisms for parameter tuning and extending the method to other types of neural networks and real-time applications.

articleTitle: Prediction of Monkeypox Disease Using Biogeography Based Optimization Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Monkeypox, a rare viral illness predominantly found in Central and West Africa, presents significant public health concerns. Detecting and predicting monkeypox outbreaks early is essential for effective disease management. In this study, we propose a new method for predicting monkeypox using Biogeography-Based Optimization (BBO) alongside machine learning techniques. We used clinical features and demographic data dataset to train and evaluate our predictive model. BBO was employed to select the most relevant subset of features from the dataset, improving the model’s performance. Our findings demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, achieving high accuracy in predicting monkeypox outbreaks. Moreover, we emphasize the importance of feature selection in enhancing the interpretability and applicability of predictive models for infectious diseases. This research contributes to advancing predictive analytics in epidemiology and offers valuable insights for disease surveillance and public health interventions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Financial Trading Strategies: A Comprehensive Sentiment Analysis Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis plays a crucial role in understanding market dynamics and making informed decisions in financial trading. This paper proposes a comprehensive sentiment analysis pipeline tailored to financial markets, integrating machine learning techniques and swarm intelligence for feature selection. The pipeline encompasses pre-processing, feature extraction, swarm-based feature selection, training, classification, and evaluation stages. Pre-processing involves text normalization techniques such as tokenization, lowercasing, and stop words removal. Feature extraction utilizes TF-IDF values and similarity measures to represent text data. Swarm intelligence algorithms are employed for feature selection, optimizing the subset of features based on classifier performance. Machine learning classifiers are trained on the selected features to predict sentiment labels, and evaluation metrics assess the pipeline’s performance. The effectiveness of the pipeline is demonstrated through experiments on financial datasets, highlighting the importance of parameter tuning and algorithmic optimization. This research contributes to advancing sentiment analysis in financial markets, providing a robust framework for decision-making in trading and investment.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Secure Coding: Revolutionizing Source Code Defense
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Secure coding is a paramount practice in software development, serving to safeguard applications against vulnerabilities and security breaches. Traditionally, this process has relied on manual analysis, a method that can be time-consuming and might overlook potential issues. This paper reviews the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically Large Language Models (LLMs), into secure coding practices, presenting an innovative approach to bolster code quality and security. The research explores the dynamic relationship between LLMs and secure coding. LLMs, equipped with advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) capabilities, possess the unique ability to comprehend code context and accurately identify vulnerabilities. They function as invaluable assistants to developers and security professionals, providing real-time guidance, offering remediation strategies, and amplifying human capabilities. While LLMs offer substantial promise, they are not without challenges. Their interpretive understanding can sometimes result in false positives and negatives. The paper underscores the importance of combining LLM insights with established security practices to establish a comprehensive and robust approach to code security.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multilingual Table-to-Text Generation with QA Blueprints: Overcoming Challenges in Low-Resource Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Limiting training data in low-resource languages is a barrier to Natural Language Processing (NLP). Regardless, languages with thousands of users worldwide require improved NLP capabilities. The Table-to-Text task—typically develops natural language descriptions using data tables, tests model reasoning abilities—although it is especially tough in multi-language settings. System output frequently lack credit to their underlying data. Intermediate planning strategies—which include Question-Answer (QA) blueprints—improving summarization tasks by presenting related QA pair prior to verbalization. Therefore, this study analyses whether QA blueprints improve multilingual Table-to-Text output attribution. An enlarged multilingual dataset, encompassing African languages, contains QA blueprints that were produced and filtered heuristically. This dataset is used to fine-tune sequence-to-sequence model (transformers)—both with and without blueprints. Two configurations are evaluated—English reference blueprints with language target verbalization and modified blueprints. These results show that English-only models benefit from blueprints, whereas multi language models cannot. Errors in machine-translating blueprints provide challenges, as do models that rely on their generated blueprints.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis for Electrical Noise Capabilities of TFET Configuration Topologies for Low Power Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Tunnel field effect transistors (TFET) have become a viable alternative to classic CMOS due to their advantages, such as substantially decreased leakage current and steeper sub-threshold slope. The paper overviews several electrical noises that might arise in a fundamental TFET device. The presence of diverse noise sources in TFET, like random telegraph noise (RTN), flicker noise, shot noise, etc., has low/high-frequency noise that affects performance across different frequency bands. A different prototype with analytical capability has been created to investigate the alteration in electrostatic potential caused by a charged trap in the oxide of the gate of TFET by changing the materials. III-V materials like $\text{Ge} / \text{Si}, \text{GaAsSb} / \text{InGaAs}$, etc., hetero-junction TFET have been analyzed to compare the Gaussian trap; a uniform trap yields a higher Ion to Ioff ratio and lower subthreshold swing. The present research also investigates the influence of electrical noise on the efficiency of different TFET configurations. This study also compares five TFET structures: Ge-based Optimized work, SiGe-S-NW-TFET, Si based nanotube TFET, Si/SiGe HTG-TFET, and Ge-Source vTFET. The Ge-based TFET achieves the highest Ion of $80.9 \mu \text{A} / \mu \text{m}$ at $\text{V}_{\text{GS}}$ is 0.55 V, while the Ge-Source vTFET exhibits the lowest SS of $21.2 \text{mV} / \text{dec}$, highlighting their potential for low-power applications.

articleTitle: Pose Fit: ML Powered Fitness Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This study explores the efficacy of MoveNet and MediaPipe frameworks in tracking Bicep Curls, Deadifts, and Squats, with the objective of enhancing fitness monitoring and promoting exercise safety. Through a comprehensive comparative analysis, the accuracy and real-time performance of these frameworks during weightlifting exercises are evaluated. The accuracy achieved with MediaPipe is 92-96% whereas with MoveNet it’s $\mathbf{8 2 - 8 8 \%}$ depending on the stability of the camera and device features. Additionally, a sophisticated mobile application is developed using Flutter, offering users a seamless interface to interact with the pose tracking models. The application facilitates exercise selection, provides real-time feedback on form and posture, and enables progress tracking. By integrating advanced pose tracking technology with mobile integration, this research aims to improve fitness experiences and mitigate the risk of injuries. The findings provide valuable insights into optimizing pose tracking frameworks for effective exercise guidance, thus contributing to the advancement of fitness technology for enhanced user outcomes and overall wellbeing. This holistic approach underscores the importance of leveraging cutting-edge technology to foster safer and more effective fitness practices.

articleTitle: GreenGuard: Advanced Sensor Solutions for Enhanced Crop Health and Growth
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This study investigates an innovative soil management approach integrating advanced sensor technology to enhance crop growth conditions. The research focuses on critical soil parameters: pH, moisture, and temperature, essential for plant health and soil quality. By employing state-of-the-art sensors, the study continuously monitors and adjusts these parameters, promoting sustainable agriculture and increased crop yields. features include real-time tracking of soil pH, providing insights into nutrient availability and microbial activity, crucial for soil health. Moisture sensors accurately measure soil water content, aiding in precise irrigation practices and preventing harmful effects of improper watering. Additionally, temperature sensors help maintain ideal conditions for microbial activity and root development. The research includes extensive experimental work to evaluate the effectiveness of this sensor-based system in enhancing plant growth and soil fertility. The results demonstrate the potential of this technology-driven approach to boost agricultural output while minimizing environmental impacts. A notable aspect of the system is an alert mechanism that informs users about significant changes in soil conditions, aiding timely crop management interventions. The paper contributes to the scientific understanding of plant-soil relationships and offers practical strategies for agricultural practitioners. It presents a comprehensive, data-centric method combining pH, moisture, and temperature sensors, paving the way for a sustainable and efficient future in agriculture.

articleTitle: GPS Integrated Landmine Detection Rover with Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking landmine detection rover equipped with ESP32 and Arduino Uno microcontrollers, marking a significant advancement in mine detection technology. Designed for swift navigation through hazardous terrain, the rover employs advanced sensors to detect landmines with high precision. It delivers accurate GPS coordinates and real-time camera monitoring through Bluetooth connectivity, ensuring comprehensive situational awareness. The rover’s robust chassis, featuring a six-wheel design, enables seamless movement over challenging terrains, further enhancing its operational effectiveness. Results demonstrate that the rover achieves a detection accuracy rate of over 95%, significantly improving safety and efficiency in mine clearance operations. This innovative vehicle is a crucial asset for both reconnaissance and humanitarian missions, providing a reliable solution in volatile environments.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Code Reviews: Leveraging Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: As the complexity and volume of software development continue to grow, the need for efficient and thorough code review processes becomes increasingly critical. This paper explores the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and Bard, into code review workflows to enhance software quality and security. By leveraging the natural language processing capabilities of LLMs, we aim to streamline the identification of code issues, detect potential security vulnerabilities, and provide developers with actionable feedback. Through a comprehensive analysis of current literature, case studies, and experimental data, this study evaluates the impact of AI-assisted code reviews on developer productivity and code quality. We also address the challenges and limitations of relying on LLMs, including context comprehension and potential biases. Our findings suggest that while LLMs offer significant advantages in automating and improving code reviews, they should complement rather than replace human expertise. This paper provides insights into best practices for integrating LLMs into development workflows, ultimately contributing to more robust and secure software systems.

articleTitle: Optimization for IoT Jobs in Multi-Cloud Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Effective network communication is essential in the current digital era, and cloud computing (CC) and the Internet of Things (IoT) are significant aspects of daily life. Accelerating and lowering the latency of data transfers to the cloud for processing, analysis, and storage is the aim of cloud computing. IoT integration and job scheduling are the two most challenging issues in the multi-cloud computing environment because of the diverse and numerous IoT devices. The significant objectives of cloud computing-based IoT optimization are to reduce the total time needed to complete all input operations, determine which resources are required for the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT), and other crucial protocols used in this work to display delay and evaluate the performance of different jobs at different IoT nodes and bit counts. Results and analysis show the viability of cloudSim is successfully achieved with the use of delayed quality of communication of jobs for different nodes.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Framework for Data Loss Prevention and Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Modern enterprises face a serious threat from data loss, or the unintentional or undesired disclosure of data. Modern Data Loss Protection (DLP) systems either discover anomalies in regular behavior (anomaly-based) or use signatures of known attack patterns. Though signature-based solutions are effective in accurately identifying known attacks and may thus be used to block them, they are unable to handle unexpected attacks or attackers who choose atypical attack vectors (such as those that are only known to insiders) to execute their attack. However, because they frequently produce a high false positive rate, anomaly-based solutions are not as useful for identifying suspicious activity. In contrast, they can identify undiscovered attacks. Our research presents a hybrid DLP system that integrates anomaly-based and signature-based approaches to facilitate both prevention and detection. Using an anomaly-based engine, the framework automatically builds a model of typical user behavior, enabling it to detect unusual transactions carried out by insiders. This is usually where anomaly-based solutions end. To prevent unwanted transactions from causing harm, our framework goes one step further by using an operator’s feedback on alarms to automatically create and update attack signatures. We manage to improve time to detect a data breach was reduced by $67 \%$, improving response efficiency.

articleTitle: Streamlining Personal Finances: An ExpenseTracker Website Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing and Advance Research in Computing (SPARC)
abstract: Expense tracker is a machine based function. The “Expense Chaser” function can simplify and improve personal money management, resulting in improved financial health and reduced stress and also it is designed to computerize the process of managing and following up on pending or overdue expenses. This function leverages a systematic algorithm that identifies expenses requiring attention based on their due dates and statuses. It uses supervised learning methods, like as neural networks or decision trees, to learn and forecast categories based on past data. Which is work by querying the database to find expenses marked as pending or overdue, and then sends timely reminders to users via email as their due dates approach or pass. Additionally, it updates the status of expenses in real-time, ensuring accurate recordkeeping. By automating these tasks, it can enhances financial management, improves user experience and maintains up-to date records, thereby promoting financial discipline and ensuring that all obligations are met efficiently. Further, it can be extended by scanning the barcode on the price tag, enhanced to reduce the effort required to enter data into the input fields. In addition to recording individual logs, it proposed to add a shared consuming group to this system in future.
